excerpt: Hexis by Bevel is an open-source "company brain" that gives a team and its AI agents shared, owner-approved knowledge, skills and tools through one MCP connection. Hexis Cloud is the hosted version. Pricing and alternatives.
content:
Hexis is a shared knowledge layer for a team and all of its AI agents. It holds three things. Context is company knowledge where every page has an owner and changes go live only when the owner approves, with every version kept. Skills are reusable instructions for agents that anyone can suggest changes to in the browser; it starts with 58 ready-made ones. Tools are hundreds of services, such as HubSpot, Notion, Jira, Linear, Google Drive, GitHub, Gmail and Zendesk, reached through a single MCP connection, with keys kept on the server so agents never see a credential.

Access rules can be set per folder, file, skill and tool for both people and their agents, and audit logs show which agent used what. Everything is stored as commits in a git repository you control. Hexis works with Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Claude Code, Codex and any agent that speaks MCP. The software is open source under the Apache-2.0 licence and can be self-hosted with Docker.

Hexis Cloud, launched on Product Hunt on 12 October 2026, is the hosted version, made because many teams, especially non-technical ones, needed help running it themselves. It finished #7 for the day with 124 upvotes. Hexis is made by Bevel (Bevelites GmbH, Munich), the team behind the UTCP tool-calling protocol; Product Hunt lists co-founder Juan Viera Garcia and Ali Raza as its makers.

We have not tested Hexis ourselves. This page brings together its official site, its GitHub README, its Product Hunt page and the official pricing pages of comparable products, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.os: Browser; self-hosting needs Docker Compose and a git repository
profile.starts_at: Free for up to 3 people; Team €10 per person a month
profile.summary_short: Open-source company brain that gives a team's AI agents shared knowledge, skills and tools through one MCP
use_cases: Giving every AI agent on a team the same approved company facts
Letting non-technical colleagues improve shared agent skills, with an owner approving changes
Connecting agents to many tools through one MCP endpoint without handing out API keys
Restricting which people and agents can see a folder, file, skill or tool
Keeping an audit trail of which agent used which tool

paragraphs: Juan Viera Garcia says the team had a great time building and open-sourcing Hexis, but after the first launch they noticed that many people needed help hosting it. Because Hexis is especially useful for non-technical teams, they decided to offer a hosted version, Hexis Cloud.

In the comments, Ali Raza, who builds Bevel and UTCP, explained why a central brain rather than a code repository: many teams began by keeping rules and skills in git, but non-technical colleagues increasingly work on skills, tools like GitHub aren't intuitive for them, and repositories can't restrict access file by file. In Hexis, skills also carry explicit versions.
launch_story.attribution: Juan Viera Garcia and Ali Raza, Bevel, on Product Hunt

fit: run several AI agents across a team and want them working from the same approved context
need access control, audit logs and data you own in git
want open source you can self-host, with a hosted option
not_fit: are a single user who just wants chat memory
want to self-host but can't run Docker and manage a git repository

pricing.intro: Hexis Cloud is priced per person in euros, excluding VAT. The open-source version is free to self-host.

plans.name: Free
plans.detail: Up to 3 people; context, skills, tools and access rules; hosted for you

plans.name: Team
plans.detail: Everything in Free; add or remove seats any time and pay only for seats used

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.detail: Uptime and support SLAs, help with security and compliance reviews, rollout support

plans.name: Self-hosted
plans.detail: Run it yourself with Docker Compose and your own git repository

notes: Trial, refund and annual-billing terms are not stated on the product page.
The page does not list security certifications such as SOC 2 or ISO 27001.

alternatives.intro: Composio is on Product Hunt's alternatives list; Mem0 and Glean cover other parts of the same need. Prices come from each product's own pricing page, checked on 14 October 2026. Review scores are Product Hunt users' own.

items.name: Composio
items.what: Connects AI agents to 1,500+ third-party tools, handling authentication and triggers
items.starts_at: Hobby free (100,000 tool calls a month); Pro $29/month
items.difference: Covers the tools layer only, without an owner-approved company knowledge base or shared skills.

items.name: Mem0
items.what: Memory layer for AI agents and apps that stores and retrieves information across conversations
items.difference: Memory per user or app through an API, rather than governed team knowledge plus skills and tool access.

items.name: Glean
items.what: Enterprise AI platform for search, answers and agents across company tools
items.difference: Closed, sold through enterprise sales. Hexis is open source, self-hostable and free for up to 3 people.

alternatives.more: Product Hunt also lists Lyzr, Switch, GraphBit and Opengeni.

liked: A hosted option, since hosting was the blocker after the first launch
Making it easier for the people who write a team's skills to take part
asked: Which agents can use it (answer: any agent that speaks MCP or UTCP)
How versions work when skills live centrally instead of in a repository (answer: skills have explicit versions)

quotes.text: Hosting was clearly the blocker, and it's nice to see it fixed.
quotes.author: Mishaal Rashid

quotes.text: A hosted option should make it easier for the people writing the team's skills to get involved.
quotes.author: Oleksii Sekundant

quotes.text: Agents and clients used by Hexis at the moment: Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, or custom agents? Anyone who can speak MCP?
quotes.author: Muhammad Ahmed

pros: Free hosted plan for up to 3 people
Owner approval and version history for knowledge and skills
One MCP endpoint for many tools; credentials stay on the server
Access rules down to a single file, plus audit logs
Data stored as git commits in a repository you control
cons: Needs MCP-capable agents to be useful
Self-hosting requires Docker and git administration
No security certifications listed on the product page
Priced in euros per person, which grows with team size

x.none: We found no independent posts about Hexis Cloud on X to link yet.

faq.a: The hosted version is free for up to 3 people, and the open-source version is free to self-host under Apache-2.0. The Team plan is €10 per person a month, excluding VAT.

faq.q: Which AI agents work with Hexis?
faq.a: Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Claude Code, Codex and any other agent that speaks MCP; a reply in the Product Hunt discussion added that agents using UTCP work too.

faq.q: Do agents see my API keys?
faq.a: No, according to Bevel. Keys stay on the Hexis server and agents reach tools through Hexis's MCP endpoint.

faq.q: Why not just keep skills in a git repository?
faq.a: Bevel's answer on Product Hunt: non-technical colleagues increasingly work on skills and find tools like GitHub hard to use, and repositories can't restrict access file by file. Hexis still stores everything as git commits in a repository you control.
Bevel (Bevelites GmbH, Munich), the team behind the UTCP tool-calling protocol.
